fatal_errors: The proposed intervention compares HEA and conventional multilayers rather than varying the HEA multilayer period to generate coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated structures.
It assumes elevated-temperature creep, whereas the target concerns room-temperature nanoindentation creep under specified loads and loading rates.

The proposed mechanism misses the central role of semicoherent interfaces, misfit-dislocation-mediated glide blocking, possible stress-induced interfacial amorphization, and the resulting transition toward diffusion or interface slip.
It does not predict the nonmonotonic optimum at a 16 nm modulation period or the associated minimum stress exponent and maximum creep resistance.
No prior evidence is cited, and the assumed coherent baseline with minimal pre-existing dislocation density is not established.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses sustained deformation in FCC/BCC HEA multilayers and offers an explicit, measurable falsification test, so it has broad problem alignment and reasonable experimental discriminability. However, it reconstructs neither the decisive structural comparison nor the target conditions. Its interfacial-dislocation accumulation mechanism is largely opposite to the target account, in which semicoherent interfaces block glide and may trigger amorphization-assisted diffusion or interface slip. The baseline also omits the coherent M8 and grain-boundary-dominated M32/M80 controls. Because the alternative mechanism is generic and unsupported by cited evidence, it is classified as unsupported rather than a well-supported plausible alternative.
